primitives.name: Per-Game Convex Aggregation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Grid WAR (GWAR): context-neutral win probability added above replacement at the point the starter exits, computed per game and summed over the season.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'GWAR': 'dimensionless aggregate WAR value', 'R_i': 'runs allowed in game i, dimensionless', 'w_rep': 'replacement level win probability, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Runs allowed follow a Poisson process; win probability is convex in runs allowed; context-neutral adjustments via empirical Bayes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When run distributions deviate significantly from Poisson or when replacement level misalignment occurs.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's per-play WPA computation where each game contributes a convexly aggregated marginal win probability, enabling scalable team valuation.
layer2.telemetry: RMSE between predicted and actual pitcher rankings.

primitives.name: Empirical Bayes Shrinkage Talent Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Pitcher talent: parametric Empirical Bayes shrinkage estimators μ̂_p (Brown 2008 style), shrunk toward the overall mean by games pitched; mapped to ranks for fair cross-metric comparison.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'μ̂_p': 'shrunken pitcher talent estimate, dimensionless', 'n_p': 'games pitched by pitcher p, dimensionless', 'τ': 'shrinkage parameter, dimensionless', '\\bar{R}_p': 'average runs allowed per game for pitcher p, dimensionless', 'μ_{\\text{overall}}': 'league average runs allowed per game, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Talent estimates are normally distributed around a global mean; shrinkage improves prediction accuracy via bias-variance tradeoff.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sample size is too small or when pitcher performance is highly variable.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE’s QB valuation pipeline to stabilize per-game performance estimates using historical averages and shrinkage coefficients.
layer2.telemetry: Rank RMSE improvement over raw per-game means.

primitives.name: Context-Neutral Win Probability Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Grid function f(I,R): P(win | R runs allowed through I complete innings), league-average offenses, estimated via Empirical Bayes Poisson model with positive-normal prior on team strength and ballpark adjustment.
primitives.latex: f(I, R) = \mathbb{P}(\text{win} | R, I) = \int_{\theta} \mathbb{P}(\text{win} | R, \theta) \cdot p(\theta | \text{data}) d\theta
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f(I, R)': 'context-neutral win probability, dimensionless', 'I': 'innings completed, dimensionless', 'R': 'runs allowed, dimensionless', 'θ': 'team strength parameters, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: League-average offense and defense; Poisson process for runs; empirical Bayes priors capture team-level variability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When league-average assumptions fail due to temporal shifts or non-Poisson run dynamics.

layer2.mapping: Adapts to NFL WPA computations by replacing baseball-specific inputs with football-specific scoring states and transition probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Out-of-sample validation against ESPN/FanGraphs win probabilities.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of Grid WAR lies in its convex aggregation principle—computing win probability contribution per game and summing rather than averaging first. This avoids Jensen's inequality-induced underestimation of true value. The Poisson/Skellam framework provides a probabilistic foundation for estimating win probability based on runs allowed, adjusted for team strength and park effects. The empirical Bayes shrinkage estimator stabilizes pitcher talent estimates by borrowing strength across players, reducing variance without introducing significant bias. These primitives form a dual structure: one for valuation (convex aggregation) and one for inference (shrinkage). The failure mode arises when assumptions about Poissonity or stationarity break down, particularly in mid-inning scenarios or with sparse data. The mapping to GSE involves adapting these concepts to NFL scoring dynamics, where win probability depends on drive outcomes rather than innings.
